h: Frank Herbert's desert-planet saga as vast, hushed, thunderous cinema: a young heir inherits a doomed fief and an empire's worth of dread.

like.r: The source novel packs in far more ecology, religion and scheming, and rewards readers who want the politics under the spectacle.
The older desert epic about an outsider swallowed by a people's destiny, with the same awe at sand and scale.
Same director, same patient, monumental sci-fi mood, trading sandworms for neon and memory.

h: The desert war arrives: an exile rises among the Fremen while love and prophecy pull him toward a future he fears; huge, loud, hypnotic.

like.r: The template for an outsider who becomes a legend among desert people, with a more ambivalent view of the myth he builds.
Another crowd-roaring epic of vengeance and empire, more earthbound and more straightforwardly rousing.
Wasteland spectacle and a cult-like war machine, stripped to one nonstop chase.

h: Three hours of physicists, hearings and fear, cut like a thriller around the man who built the bomb and then had to live beside it.

like.r: The biography the film is drawn from, with far more depth on his private life, his politics and his fall.
Another brilliant, flawed founder told through depositions and talk that crackles like action.
The same nuclear dread played as black comedy rather than tragedy.

h: A candy-colored plastic paradise cracks when its heroine starts thinking about death; a loud, sincere, self-mocking comedy about being a woman.

like.r: Another pastel, quotable comedy with a sweetly clueless heroine who learns something real.
Also about a perfect manufactured world and the hero who notices the seams, but with a gentler, sadder tone.
Pink-clad optimism that refuses to be underestimated, lighter and more conventional.

h: A tired laundromat owner is flung across universes in a kung-fu, hot-dog-fingers, bagel-shaped riot that turns out to be about mothers and daughters.

like.r: Another deadpan high-concept oddity where an absurd portal exposes ordinary loneliness.

like.t: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
like.r: Inventive reality-bending whose weirdness serves a heartbreak, quieter and less frantic.
The multiverse-hopping, kung-fu forerunner, played with pure seriousness rather than silliness.
Hyperactive, gag-per-second genre mash-up with video-game logic and a sweet center.

h: On a remote Irish island a man is dumped by his best friend for being dull, and the feud grows absurdly cruel, funny and sad.

like.r: Same writer-director and same pairing of low-key jokes with moral weight, in a hitman setup.
Small-town grievance turned bleakly funny, angrier and more plot-heavy.
Another Irish coastal community, darkly witty talk around a weighty moral question.

h: A celebrated conductor's control over an orchestra and everyone near her starts to crumble; icy, ambiguous, built on long dialogue scenes.

like.r: Another study of music, perfectionism and abusive mastery, with louder drums and more direct sparring.
Art-world ambition tipping into paranoia, but pulpier and more openly horrific.
A magnetic, monstrous leader who is both genius and wreck, told with the same icy patience.

h: A grown woman replays a cheap Turkish holiday with her young father through camcorder fragments, noticing what her child self could not.

like.r: Another hushed, impressionistic portrait where what goes unsaid carries the pain.
Quiet grief and a damaged adult, more talky and more explicit about what happened.
A damaged father, a child, and a story assembled slowly from silences and old home-movie images.

h: Two childhood sweethearts from Seoul meet again twenty-four years apart in New York; a tender, restrained film about the lives not lived.

like.r: Another talk-your-way-into-love story with a clock ticking, lighter and more youthful.
Longing expressed through glances and restraint, more stylized and just as aching.
Two lonely people connecting in a foreign city, wry and dreamlike.
Two people who keep finding and missing each other across years, told with the same quiet honesty.

h: A woman revived with a baby's brain learns the world at gleeful speed, in a fish-eyed storybook Europe full of grotesques and appetite.

like.r: The source novel is a nested, illustrated Victorian hoax with a very different structure and a sharper political edge.
The original made-creature story, grimmer and more tragic where the film is bawdy and liberated.
Same director's courtly, mean comedy of power, with equally strange framing.
Another handmade, absurd dystopia full of contraptions and bureaucratic cruelty.

h: Oil-rich Osage families are picked off one by one by the white neighbors who smile at them; a long, sorrowful crime epic with no hero.

like.r: The reported book behind the film, structured as a detective story and more pointed about the FBI.

like.t: Once Upon a Time in America
like.r: Another long, melancholic gangster saga about greed and betrayal across decades.
Oil, money and rot in the American West, more intimate and operatic.
The same director's crime world, but fast, funny and seductive where this one is sorrowful.

h: A grumpy teacher, a grieving cook and a stuck-behind student share a prep school over Christmas break; wry, warm, and shot like a 1970s film.

like.r: Another New England boys' school story about a teacher who changes a student, more rousing and less cranky.
Same director's bittersweet comedy of sour, lovable middle-aged men on a road.
A prep-school comedy of an eccentric kid and a melancholy older mentor, more mannered and stylized.
A gifted, wounded young man and a damaged mentor, more overtly emotional.

h: A widow lives in a van and follows seasonal work across the American West, among real nomads, in a film that breathes more than it plots.

like.t: Nomadland: Surviving America in the Twenty-First Century
like.r: The reporting that inspired the film, broader and angrier about the economics behind van life.
Another journey out of ordinary life into the open land, more romantic and more tragic.
A drifter crossing desert landscapes in a spare, melancholy road movie.
A small, hard-luck wanderer story told with the same unforced realism.

h: A woman who pretends to be drunk in bars to punish predators has a deeper reason; bubblegum colors on top of a furious, grieving thriller.

like.r: Another glossy thriller where a woman's rage and strategy drive the plot and the audience's sympathies keep shifting.
A different era's story of women answering male violence, warmer and more open-road.
A pastel-toned, deadpan revenge comedy with a similarly mean sense of humor.

h: A lazy would-be knight accepts a beheading game and rides toward an answer; strange, painterly Arthurian myth that refuses a tidy hero's arc.

like.r: A medieval knight on a journey that ends in a reckoning with death, black-and-white and more philosophical.
Another dreamlike, mud-and-mist Arthurian vision, more bombastic.

like.t: Monty Python and the Holy Grail
like.r: The same legend played as slapstick, if you want the other extreme.

h: A teenage hustler and a twenty-something assistant drift in and out of each other's orbits through 1973 San Fernando Valley hustles.

like.r: Same director's 1970s Valley ensemble, more sprawling and darker.
A teenager in a 1970s world of adults, nostalgic and sweet.

like.t: Once Upon a Time in Hollywood
like.r: Another loose, hangout-style love letter to old Los Angeles.
A hangout movie in a 1970s summer with a big ensemble cast, plotless and affectionate.

h: A young, damaged Batman hunts a riddle-leaving killer through a rain-soaked Gotham in a three-hour detective noir.

like.r: Rain, clues and a ritual killer with a scheme; the model for this darker detective Gotham.
Another grounded Gotham, but more heist-like and focused on a charismatic villain.
The graphic-novel take on a young, flawed Batman and a corrupt city, in a tighter format.

h: An aging pilot trains young hotshots for an impossible mission; real jets, sincere sentiment and a finale built entirely out of speed.

like.r: The glossy original that set up the characters and the swagger, if you want the pre-history.
Practical stunts and relentless propulsion, in a far weirder world.
Aerial combat and a mission countdown, colder and more experimental.

h: Two tennis friends and the woman who split them collide in one match, cut across a decade; sweaty, thumping and very flirtatious.

like.r: Tennis, class and desire collapsing into a thriller, chillier and more fatalistic.
Another drive-to-be-the-best story edited like combat and punctuated by pounding rhythm.
A friendship strained by a shared attraction, rawer and more road-trip.

h: A Brooklyn dancer impulsively marries a Russian oligarch's son and the fairy tale turns to screaming farce, then somewhere unexpectedly tender.

like.r: The Cinderella fantasy this film takes apart, much softer and sweeter.
Another New York hustle played at a panic pitch, with an equally exhausting energy.
Same director's warm, unglamorous eye on people at the economic edge.

h: A Hungarian architect rebuilds his life in postwar America under a patron who owns him; a long, imposing, intermission-split epic.

like.r: Another American rise-and-ruin story built on obsession and a magnetic, unnerving score.
The other famous architect-versus-patron story, far more didactic and pro-ego.
A European artist surviving history's violence, told with spare, restrained humanity.

h: Behind sealed doors a cardinal runs a papal election while secrets surface; a glossy ecclesiastical thriller with a satisfying last reveal.

like.r: The novel behind the film: the same election, with more procedure and inner reflection.
Another look at the human beings behind the Vatican's pageantry, warmer and talkier.
Another closed-world whodunit of institutional suspicion, quieter and denser.
A grounded drama about the Church's hidden failings, told through reporters.

h: Twin brothers open a juke joint in 1932 Mississippi and the music draws something hungry; blues, history and vampire siege, all in one night.

like.r: Another single-night bar siege that swerves from crime story into monsters, trashier and funnier.
Horror used to look at race and American history, tighter and more satirical.
Another Depression-era Mississippi where roots music is the soul of the story, played as comedy.

h: A cruel, charismatic Montana rancher torments his brother's new family; a western of dust, repression and slowly unfolding menace.

like.r: The novel is leaner and drier, a short Western that reads like a coiled threat.
Another Western about hidden desire in a world of hard men, far more tender.
Another study of a domineering man in a harsh landscape, loud where this is hushed.
Same director's earlier frontier story, with silence, longing and violent passion.

h: Two astronomers warn that a comet will destroy Earth and nobody cares; a broad, furious comedy about media, politics and denial.

like.r: The classic comedy of leaders failing to stop the end of the world, sharper and colder.
A cruder, dumber, lower-budget view of a society that has stopped listening to experts.
Another satire of television turning everything into spectacle, with more bite.
Same director's cynical, fast-cut explanation of insiders who saw the collapse coming.

h: A Viking prince grows up with a single vow: kill the uncle who murdered his father; mud, ritual, volcanic landscapes and gory saga.

like.r: The revenge story that descends from the same Scandinavian legend, much more talky and doubting.
A harsher, more hallucinatory vision of Norse violence, far sparser.
Vengeance for a murdered family on the grand scale, glossier and more crowd-pleasing.

h: An Oxford scholarship boy is welcomed into a glamorous family's country house for a summer, and his fascination turns uncomfortable.

like.r: The classic outsider who insinuates himself into a glittering life, sunnier and more suspenseful.
The elegiac old-money Oxford and country-house novel this film wickedly updates.
A college outsider drawn into a privileged circle with a dark secret, more literary and slower.
Another story of an outsider infiltrating a rich household, with sharper class satire.

h: A housebound, severely obese teacher tries to reconnect with his estranged teenage daughter in a week of cramped, painful conversations.

like.r: Same director's tender portrait of a broken body and a failed father, rawer and more physical.
Another study of a man crushed by loss trying to relate to a young relative.
The novel the teacher keeps coming back to, an obsessive giant of a book.

h: A botched spell brings villains from other Spider-Man eras into one story; a fan-service crowd-pleaser with a surprisingly sad core.

like.r: The much-loved earlier Spider-Man that treats a hero's personal cost with warmth and humor.
Another big crossover payoff that rewards fans with callbacks.
A fun, family-friendly tale of tampering with the timeline.

h: A tech billionaire invites his old friends to a private Greek island for a murder game, and a real death follows; sunny, sly and baroque.

like.r: The model for an eccentric detective with a closed circle of suspects, drier and more traditional.
Another murder-mystery parlor game played as slapstick.
A country-house whodunit with a huge ensemble and class barbs, more languid.

h: A spy learns that bullets and bodies can move backward through time, in a globe-trotting thriller that demands repeat viewings to untangle.

like.r: Same director's heist-in-layers puzzle, much easier to follow and more emotional.
A no-budget time-travel film as dense as this one, but talky, grimy and garage-scaled.
A time-travel action story that keeps the rules clear and cares more about the characters.

h: Wealthy diners are ferried to a private island for a tasting menu whose courses grow ever stranger; a sleek, mean-spirited satire of fine dining.

like.r: Another class-war thriller in a single house with a savagely funny first half.
The real-life, reverent counterpart to this movie's obsessive chef.
Another satire where the rich are trapped, humiliated and stripped of status, less thriller and more farce.

h: Models, oligarchs and a fed-up cleaning lady meet on a luxury yacht, then a storm and a desert island flip the pecking order.

like.r: A cleverer, tighter class-reversal story with more suspense and less cringe.
Same director's art-world satire, built on the same embarrassing social experiments.
The classic about order collapsing on an island once the rules of the old world vanish.

h: A boy discovers movies as a way of seeing, and of seeing what he would rather not, while his parents' marriage frays in suburban Arizona.

like.r: Another love letter to film seen through a childhood, more sentimental and Italian.
A coming-of-age story that watches a family change, steadier and plotless.

like.t: Close Encounters of the Third Kind
like.r: The earlier Spielberg suburban-family film where obsession and wonder break a household.

h: Silent-era Hollywood in a drunken, drug-soaked frenzy as the talkies arrive and everyone's careers turn over; over three hours, in overdrive.

like.r: Another ensemble rise-and-fall of an entertainment industry, with equal excess and more warmth.
The sunny musical version of the same silent-to-sound transition.
A bitter, tidy noir about Hollywood chewing up its own.
Another long, loud descent through greed and excess, with the same sweaty energy.

h: The King's rise and trap told by his manipulative manager, in a rhinestoned whirl of cuts, concerts and Luhrmann's trademark excess.

like.r: Same director's hyper-kinetic, tragic musical pageant.
A more conventional but warm music-legend biopic of the same era.
Another glitzy, fantasy-tinged rock biopic about stardom and its costs.

h: Four journalists drive toward a collapsing Washington, D.C., through an American landscape of checkpoints and snipers; cold, loud and unsettling.

like.r: Another river-trip descent into madness, longer and more hallucinatory.
A near-future society breaking down, filmed in long, immersive takes.
A journalist's-eye view of a country at war with itself, angrier and rougher.

h: A scruffy Minnesotan arrives in Greenwich Village in 1961 and turns the folk scene upside down before it can claim him.

like.r: A fictional folk singer in the same Village, rueful and unsuccessful where this one is a star.
A deliberately fractured, experimental portrait of the same artist.
The documentary of the singer on tour, direct and unpolished.

h: A girl stolen from a hidden paradise grows up in the wasteland's warlord wars; a sprawling revenge saga that spans years, not one chase.

like.r: The leaner, pared-back classic that defined this world and its vehicular mayhem.
A single-minded, stylized revenge quest by a woman, more playful and referential.
Another action film built around a fierce heroine and relentless set pieces.

h: On a doomed ice-planet colony a hapless 'expendable' is killed for experiments and reprinted each time; a gooey, silly, political sci-fi comedy.

like.r: The source novel is drier and more cerebral, with a different ending and creature design.
Same director's class-struggle sci-fi, grimmer and more action-heavy.
Another story about a lonely worker and his replaceable self, quiet and melancholy.

h: An ex-revolutionary dad hiding in a haze of weed is dragged back into old fights when a military enemy hunts his daughter; a manic, big-budget chase.

like.r: The loose source, a shaggy-dog novel of aging radicals, paranoia and parents, far more digressive.
Another stoned, funny, plot-tangled L.A. odyssey with a shambling hero.
Another anarchic satire about violence and revolt, bleaker and less warm.

h: A washed-up racer comes back to coach a rookie on a struggling Grand Prix team; shot on real tracks with real roar, but a familiar underdog story.

like.r: A better-drawn and more dramatic Formula One rivalry, based on real drivers.
Another crowd-pleasing racing movie about two mismatched men and a corporate obstacle.
The documentary version of the sport's glory and danger, assembled entirely from archive footage.

h: A New York matchmaker who prices people like assets must choose between a rich suitor and her broke ex; a cool-headed look at love as a market.

like.r: Same director's quieter, more wistful take on love and what we leave behind.
The classic New York comedy of talk and timing, warmer and more conventional.
A clear-eyed New York story about what love costs, much sadder.

h: A professor on a Greek holiday watches a young mother on the beach and is pulled back to the choices that shaped her own motherhood.

like.r: The terse novel behind the film, with the same frank, uncomfortable interior voice.
Two women alone by the sea, whose identities start to blur, more abstract.
A similarly unsparing look at the cost of choosing yourself in a family.

h: A nine-year-old watches his street turn violent in 1969 as his family weighs leaving; a warm, film-loving childhood memory shot in black and white.

like.r: Another autobiographical child's-eye view of a community under threat, funnier and more comic.
A black-and-white childhood memory of a household during political unrest, more austere.
A bleaker Irish childhood memoir with the same comic voice in hard times.

h: Three articles and an obituary from a fictional American magazine in a French town, staged as dollhouse tableaux with a huge cast.

like.r: Same director's more propulsive, funnier storybook caper.
Anderson's family portrait with more heart and a stronger sad streak.
Another whimsical, color-saturated, devotedly Parisian fantasy.

h: Shakespeare's murderous couple on stark, shadowed stages of fog and angular sets, in black-and-white that feels like a nightmare.

like.r: The play itself, whose verse is trimmed but not rewritten here.
The Japanese reworking of the same tale, with fog, spirits and Noh-style stillness.
A bloodier, muddier, more earthy version of the same tragedy.

h: A drifter learns the carnival mentalist's tricks and takes them uptown to rob the rich; a rich, rotting noir of cons and consequences.

like.r: The pulp novel behind both film versions, short, bleak and merciless.
The model noir of a man talked into a doomed scheme by a woman, leaner.
Another moral-fog classic with shadow-slashed cinematography.

h: An elderly man's flat keeps rearranging itself as dementia scrambles his sense of who is who; we live inside his confusion, with no guide.

like.r: Another painfully intimate view of an old person's decline, colder and more observational.
A novel from inside early-onset Alzheimer's, plain and compassionate.
Another film that makes us share a memory-damaged mind, as a thriller.

h: Two wedding guests find themselves trapped in the same day forever and cope by drinking, flirting and slowly falling in love; breezy and sweet.

like.r: The original time-loop comedy that this one riffs on, with a gentler redemption arc.
The action-movie time loop, with the same repeated deaths played for suspense.

like.t: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
like.r: A romance bent by sci-fi, sadder and more inventive.

h: A drunken screenwriter dictates Citizen Kane from a bed in the desert, in flashbacks to a studio-era Hollywood of mogul feuds and wisecracks.

like.r: The film that is being written, with the same nonlinear structure.
Another black-and-white Hollywood insider story, bitter and noir.
A comedic nightmare of a writer in the 1940s studio system.

h: Anti-war activists face an openly biased judge after the 1968 Democratic Convention; a fast, jokey courtroom drama.

like.r: Another snappy Sorkin-scripted courtroom drama driven by a big confrontation.
A classic of ideas on trial, with a lawyer facing a hostile court.
A civil-rights-era look at organizers pushing against the state, more reverent.

h: A stargazers' convention in a pastel desert town is interrupted by an alien; a play-within-a-play about grief and being stuck.

like.r: Anderson's gentler and more romantic storybook about kids and adults.

like.t: Close Encounters of the Third Kind
like.r: The earnest, awestruck version of a small community meeting visitors.
Another stylized 1950s-flavored town where something strange shakes up ordinary lives.

h: A frustrated literary novelist writes a cynical, stereotype-laden book as a joke and it becomes a hit; a satire with a family drama at its heart.

like.r: The sharper, stranger source novel, with an even more bruising satirical streak.
Another satire on race and selling out, wilder, absurdist and angrier.
A landmark of American race comedy-drama set over one day.

h: An actress shadows the woman she will play, a notorious wife with a past, and the picnic-perfect household begins to wobble.

like.r: The original film about a woman studying another woman until the two blur.
A sharp, witty tale of an admirer who gets too close to her idol.
Another teacher-and-student scandal drama, seen through a manipulative observer.

h: A conductor and an actress build a marriage around his talent and his secrets over decades; swooning camera, a prosthetic nose, real music.

like.r: Same director's romance between two artists, with similar long close-ups.
A more operatic, flamboyant music-world drama with a lot of conducting.
A different artist couple, with an emphasis on how people stay or split.

h: A shoe-company scout bets everything on an unproven rookie in 1984; a boardroom sports movie that is all talk, tracksuits and synth.

like.r: Another sports story fought in offices and spreadsheets instead of on the field.
A sports-agent comedy-drama with a similar underdog, quotable energy.
A dialogue-fueled tale of an upstart business win, much colder.

h: The Von Erich brothers wrestle for a father who treats them as projects, and tragedy keeps arriving; a sorrowful, tender sports drama.

like.r: Another true wrestling story of control and brotherly bonds, colder and creepier.
A raw, sad portrait of a body and a career broken by the ring.
A classic of a family that cannot talk about its grief.

h: Five years with two Chicago teenagers who hope basketball will lift them out; the game is only the frame for a story of school, money and family.

like.r: Another look at a town pinning its hopes on teenage athletes, more journalistic and broader in scope.
Another film that follows young people over years of real time, as fiction and gentler.
A more polemical documentary on the systems that shape the lives Hoop Dreams follows.

h: Interviews, reenactments and a hypnotic Philip Glass score re-open a Texas police-killing case and show how a man ended up on death row.

like.r: The classic nonfiction novel of a murder case, written with the same fascination for killers and cops.
The fiction classic about conflicting versions of a crime, playing the same unreliable-testimony game.
Another documentary where the truth of a criminal case keeps shifting under the camera.

h: A mother and daughter, relatives of a famous family, live in a decaying mansion full of cats and raccoons; funny, vain, tender and a little frightening.

like.r: Another faded star shut in a ruined mansion, in fiction with more menace.

like.t: What Ever Happened to Baby Jane?
like.r: Two aging women trapped in a house and in an old rivalry, in grand camp.
A comic, offbeat look at eccentrics who refuse to behave.

h: A Frenchman and his crew sneak into the World Trade Center to string a wire between the towers; a heist story whose payoff is pure poetry.

like.r: Another real-life physical feat retold by its survivors, with reenactments and much less joy.
The same story dramatized with Hollywood effects and a vertigo-inducing finale.
A suave crew-assembling caper with that same fun of watching a plan come together.

h: A climber prepares to scale Yosemite's El Capitan with no rope; the camera crew worries what they will film, and you will too.

like.r: A mountain tale of survival where the stakes are just as stark, told in retrospect.
The classic book on obsession and death at high altitude, more reflective and more tragic.
Another film of someone risking their life for a dream, playful where this is intense.

h: Over nine hours of interviews with survivors, perpetrators and bystanders, and no archive footage; a vast, patient act of testimony.

like.r: A short first-hand memoir of the camps, plain and devastating.
A survivor's exact, lucid account of Auschwitz, more analytic.
The dramatized, narrative counterpart to the Holocaust's story.

h: The Harlem drag balls of the 1980s, seen through the houses and the performers who built families and fantasies out of fashion, shade and survival.

like.r: A lyrical drama of Black queer life, quieter and more interior.
A history of how movies portrayed queer people, with an archive-driven wit.
A scruffy, funny fictional day with trans women on the margins of Los Angeles.

h: Aging Indonesian death-squad leaders are invited to re-stage their murders as Hollywood fantasies, with chilling and bizarre results.

like.r: The classic essay on how ordinary men commit enormous crimes, a theory for what the film shows.
Another documentary that confronts atrocity head-on through testimony, solemn and without irony.
A fiction film of violence and moral collapse, equally hallucinatory.

h: Talking Heads build their show one musician at a time on a bare stage; a concert film where the staging, funk and big suit are the story.

like.r: Another landmark concert film, more elegiac and more rooted in rock history.
A celebratory film made of long-hidden concert footage, with the same pure joy.
A fictional rock drama from the same year, with a Prince-fueled live set.

h: Unseen footage of the 1969 Harlem Cultural Festival pairs astonishing performances with the voices of Black New Yorkers who were there.

like.r: Another concert film that lets the music carry everything, more theatrical.
The same summer's better-known festival, more hippie than Harlem.
A more angry, explicitly political documentary on the same struggle.

h: A dense, furious essay-film that traces how a constitutional loophole turned slavery into mass incarceration, with scholars and archive footage.

like.r: The book behind much of this argument, more detailed and just as angry.
Another essay-film of American racism, built from James Baldwin's words.
A dramatized story of a lawyer fighting wrongful convictions, more hopeful.

h: Nearly eight hours that place a football star's fall inside decades of Los Angeles race relations, police violence and celebrity.

like.r: A shorter, angrier film on the justice system and race.
A satirical novel about race, media and justice in a big city.
Another long, humane documentary where American sport and race intertwine.

h: Two South African fans hunt for the vanished Detroit singer whose records became the soundtrack of apartheid-era protest; part mystery, part fable.

like.r: Another film about gifted musicians the spotlight missed, more ensemble-driven.
A fictional singer whom the world doesn't notice, wry and unsentimental.
A fond fictional look at 1970s music life, warmer and funnier.

h: An elderly Tokyo sushi master and his sons make the same dishes a little better each day; serene, gorgeous and a bit exhausting to watch.

like.r: The loud, profane opposite on the same subject: restaurant kitchens and the people who live in them.
A comic ode to the pursuit of the perfect bowl of ramen.
A twisted fiction about chef perfectionism taken too far.

h: The gentle children's TV host, remembered through colleagues and clips; a quiet argument that kindness can be radical.

like.r: A biography of Fred Rogers with more of the private man and his craft.
Another warm, uplifting documentary about an unlikely hero.
Another tender documentary built on patience and attention.

h: No dialogue, only time-lapse landscapes and cities set to a pulsing Philip Glass score; a wordless meditation on a world out of balance.

like.r: A similar wordless global montage, more spiritual, more beautiful and less accusatory.
Another film that uses image and music rather than talk to ask big questions.
The silent city-symphony forebear of its montage approach.

h: Herzog sifts through the footage of a man who lived among Alaskan bears and died among them, with awe, pity and a dissenting view of nature.

like.r: Another account of a man who sought meaning in the wilderness and met its indifference.
Herzog's fiction about a dreamer and his mad obsession in the jungle.
A gentler, warmer way of befriending a wild animal.

h: A burned-out filmmaker dives daily into a South African kelp forest and befriends an octopus; sweet, strange and easy to cry over.

like.r: The best-known book on octopus minds, with more science and more affection.
Another nature documentary that follows a single animal drama, more classic and narrated.
A darker, more skeptical film about a man and his bond with wild animals.

h: A day in Soviet cities captured with split screens, double exposures and speed ramps; a silent film about the act of making film.

like.r: A modern descendant that also builds meaning from montage.
Another silent-era look at the machine city, in fiction and with monumental sets.
The other great Soviet silent, built on montage but for storytelling.

h: A filmmaker assembles a scrapbook for a murdered friend's baby son, then the case takes a turn that no scrapbook could hold; devastating.

like.r: Another documentary where a family story slides toward a criminal case.
A cooler, more analytic look at a murder case and the justice system.
A true-crime classic told by a writer who knew the killer personally.

h: Michael Moore wanders America asking why it kills itself with guns, mixing prank interviews, cartoons and a sincere sense of grief.

like.r: Moore's first film, a leaner and funnier story of a factory town's abandonment.
Another personality-driven documentary that turns a social problem into a stunt.
A calmer, more thoughtful documentary on American power.

h: Robert McNamara looks back on firebombing and Vietnam in one long interview, and the film wonders how much he admits and how much he evades.

like.r: Morris's earlier film, also built on interviews and music, about a single case.
The comic nightmare version of Cold War decision-making.
The classic book on how clever men led America into Vietnam.

h: A Long Island family is torn apart by child-abuse accusations, with home videos the family kept filming; the film never tells you what to conclude.

like.r: A more formal and stylized look at a miscarriage of justice.
A very personal true-crime documentary, more emotional and more sure of its verdict.
The play about communal hysteria and accusations that can't be undone.

h: A filmmaker eats only at McDonald's for a month while doctors watch his health slide; a stunt that kicked off a food-industry debate.

like.r: The investigative book on how fast food reshaped America, more rigorous and less jokey.
Another stunt-driven, personality-led documentary that wants to provoke.
A more sober documentary on the industrial food system.

h: Al Gore presents his climate slideshow to audiences around the world, cut with scenes from his own life; plain, urgent and widely argued over.

like.r: The book that began the modern environmental movement, written with moral clarity.
A more reported, global view of how humans are changing life on Earth.
Another issue documentary built to change minds, more emotional.

h: The Brazilian Formula One champion told only through race footage and archive clips, with no talking heads, and building toward a tragic weekend.

like.r: A fictionalized F1 rivalry from the same era, in a more conventional biopic style.
The same director's archive-built portrait of another talent consumed by fame.
Another film about an athlete willing to risk everything.

h: A hapless Frenchman films street artists and then becomes one himself; whether it's true, a prank or both is part of the joke.

like.r: The earlier essay-film that also blurs truth, forgery and showmanship.
A dry fictional take on art-world pretension and outsiders.
Another film about street-level public art, but affectionate rather than prank-filled.

h: A captive orca at SeaWorld kills a trainer, and former trainers explain what captivity does to such animals; built like a thriller.

like.r: Another activist documentary, structured like a heist, about marine mammals.
A loving counterpoint to how we treat the sea's intelligent creatures.
The classic obsession with a great whale, long and symbolic rather than reportorial.

h: The backup singers behind famous hits, who sang the voices you remember, talk about wanting a spotlight of their own; joyful and a little sad.

like.r: Another story of unsung talent, centered on a single mystery.

like.t: Standing in the Shadows of Motown
like.r: A closely related documentary about the session musicians behind Motown.
The opposite, darker side of musical fame.

h: A woman in a North Macedonian village keeps wild bees and cares for her ailing mother until noisy neighbors arrive; patient and unforced.

like.r: Another fiction film shot with real people and landscapes, with a similar observational calm.
The silent ancestor of documentary-on-a-hard-life, more staged.
Another documentary about rural people, lighter and more playful.

h: An elderly director and a young street artist drive a photo truck through French villages, pasting giant portraits of the people they meet.

like.r: Varda's earlier road documentary about people who live off what others throw away.
Varda's famous fiction film about a Paris afternoon, more anxious and stylish.
Another Frenchy, whimsical celebration of small kindnesses, in fiction.

h: The jazz-voiced Camden singer, from teenage home videos to the glare of the tabloids; her songs narrate a life already slipping from her.

like.r: Same director and same archive-only method, applied to a racing driver.
Another intimate, tragic portrait of a music icon built from home material.
The fictional version of talent and addiction in the spotlight.
